answer_text:
Looking at this problem, I need to analyze how the three altitudes of an acute triangle divide it into six smaller triangles.

## Setting Up the Six Triangles

Let the triangle be $ABC$ (counterclockwise) with orthocenter $H$. The altitude feet are $D$ on $BC$, $E$ on $AC$, $F$ on $AB$. The six triangles in counterclockwise order around $H$ are:

- $t_1 = [HAE]$, $t_2 = [HFA]$, $t_3 = [HBF]$, $t_4 = [HDB]$, $t_5 = [HCD]$, $t_6 = [HEC]$

## Expressing Areas in Terms of $\tan A, \tan B, \tan C$

Let $p = \tan A$, $q = \tan B$, $r = \tan C$. For an acute triangle, $p, q, r > 0$ and $p + q + r = pqr$.

The three triangles at the orthocenter have areas:
$$[ABH] = \frac{r}{p+q+r} = \frac{1}{pq}, \quad [BCH] = \frac{1}{qr}, \quad [CAH] = \frac{1}{pr}$$

Splitting each using the altitude foot ratios (e.g., $t_2/t_3 = AF/FB = \tan B/\tan A$):

$$t_1 = \frac{1}{p(p+r)},\quad t_2 = \frac{1}{p(p+q)},\quad t_3 = \frac{1}{q(p+q)}$$
$$t_4 = \frac{1}{q(q+r)},\quad t_5 = \frac{1}{r(q+r)},\quad t_6 = \frac{1}{r(p+r)}$$

**Verification:** $t_1+t_2+t_3+t_4+t_5+t_6 = \frac{1}{pq}+\frac{1}{qr}+\frac{1}{pr} = \frac{p+q+r}{pqr} = 1$ ✓

## Computing $t_1t_3t_5 + t_2t_4t_6$

$$t_1t_3t_5 = \frac{1}{pqr\,(p+r)(p+q)(q+r)}$$

$$t_2t_4t_6 = \frac{1}{pqr\,(p+q)(q+r)(p+r)}$$

These are **identical**! So:

$$t_1t_3t_5 + t_2t_4t_6 = \frac{2}{pqr(p+q)(q+r)(r+p)} = 5$$

This gives: $pqr(p+q)(q+r)(r+p) = \dfrac{2}{5}$
